title: Canvas preview for Bevel, GradientGlow, GradientBevel, and AdjustColor filters
description:
The FiltersPanel and SWF encoder support all 7 Flash 8 filters, but the authoring-stage canvas renderer (packages/core/src/engine/renderer.ts applyFilters()) silently skips four of them:
- BevelFilter — explicitly commented 'not yet rendered'
- GradientGlowFilter — not handled
- GradientBevelFilter — not handled
- AdjustColorFilter (Brightness/Contrast/Saturation/Hue) — not handled

Only BlurFilter, DropShadowFilter, and GlowFilter produce visible results in the authoring canvas. Authors setting any of the four unrendered filters get no feedback until they publish.

Scope:
1. AdjustColor: apply a CSS filter string (brightness/contrast/saturate/hue-rotate) or a manual pixel-level color-matrix pass using an offscreen canvas. CSS filters: brightness(b) contrast(c) saturate(s) hue-rotate(h). Map Flash -100..100/hue -180..180 to CSS percentages/degrees.
2. Bevel: approximate with two ctx.shadowColor passes (highlight above-left, shadow below-right) similar to how drop-shadow works.
3. GradientGlow / GradientBevel: approximate with a single ctx.shadowColor using the first/last gradient stop colors and the filter's blurX/Y/distance/angle params.

All approximations are acceptable — exact per-pixel fidelity is a stretch goal; the goal is that authors get recognizable visual feedback. The SWF output is already correct (filters.ts encodes all 7 filter IDs properly).

Acceptance: manual test — place a shape with each of the 4 filter types, verify the authoring canvas shows a visible change (not identical to the shape with no filter applied).
